title: PowerShell Script Block Containing Reflective Loading Terminology
detection_hypothesis: If code is loaded reflectively to avoid writing a file to disk, the logged script block will contain assembly loading and dynamic invocation terminology.

field_semantics.ScriptBlockText: Decoded PowerShell script block text as executed.

collection_prerequisites: Script block logging is enabled through Group Policy or registry configuration.
PowerShell operational log collection is enabled on the endpoint.
expected_collection_gaps: PowerShell version 2 engines do not emit script block logs.
Very large script blocks are split across multiple events.
normalization_assumptions: ScriptBlockText contains the decoded script text as executed.
ingestion_differences: Multi-part script blocks may need reassembly before matching.
Some pipelines strip newlines from ScriptBlockText.
retention_considerations: Script block logging is moderate to high volume; 90 days is a common target.
false_positive_strategy: Benign matches come from a small number of engineering and vendor modules with stable script paths. Tune on the Path field and the executing host role.
tuning_guidance: Exclude the specific module path on build hosts only. Excluding the assembly load terminology globally removes the entire detection.
test_strategy: Positive cases include assembly loading and dynamic delegate creation. Negative cases use ordinary type usage, module import, and a comment that mentions reflection.
unmapped_defensive_objects_reason: No Detection Strategy, Analytic, or Data Component identifier for this technique was present in the pinned ATT&CK extraction used by this lab. Defensive arrays are left empty rather than populated with unverified identifiers. Unmapped techniques: T1620.
